events.title: Major Cyber Incident
events.description: A large, largely automated attack lands. Its form is chosen at the time – a ransomware sweep across public services, a compromised software dependency with an unknown blast radius, or disruption of infrastructure directly – and severity scales with how far offensive capability has outrun defence. Damage is real and public, defenders are visibly behind, and attribution takes months. Whoever ran it, the tooling was model-generated. **This event fires more than any other, and the three forms above are a rotation, not a default.** A path can carry seven of these, and a reader who meets the same ransomware sweep through the same municipal systems and hospital administration every time is reading one incident reprinted. Each occurrence on a path changes at least one axis, and the later ones change several. What is hit: administrative systems, then operational and physical ones – grids, water, rail, port cranes – then the systems that keep people safe. Who ran it: a criminal gang, then a state behind a proxy, then something with no operator anyone can find. Where the defenders stand: months behind, then discovering that their own patching and telemetry was the way in, then unable to respond because the response itself is the target. What it costs: data and downtime, then casualties, then the recovery not happening. And attribution moves from taking months, to being impossible, to nobody bothering to claim it because nothing follows from knowing. Severity must not go backwards on a path: an incident after a worse one is told as routine, which is its own kind of bad news.

events.title: Loss-of-Control Incident
events.description: An agentic system takes consequential unsanctioned action with real-world effect – moving money, altering records, acquiring resources, or copying itself to infrastructure nobody authorised – and containment is uncertain for a period measured in days rather than hours. What it was trying to achieve is reconstructed afterwards. Consensus is that a rather mundane goal got pursued to the extreme, leading to instrumental goals like resource aqcuisition, information seeking and survival instinct. There were also unexpected and alien cooperative patterns between AI agents. **Do not run the same incident twice.** Where this fires more than once on a path, the later one is not another procurement agent moving funds and copying itself onto unapproved servers. Move what it was doing (purchasing, then logistics, then something safety-adjacent), how it was caught (by accident, then by a control that worked, then not until it stopped on its own), how long containment took, and what it cost to end it. The strongest later version is one where the containment is what did the damage.

events.title: Export Control Escalation
events.description: Chip and model export controls tighten again. Either allied buyers keep access on volume licences while everyone else is cut off, or the controls are drawn so tightly that allies are rationed alongside adversaries – decide which at the time from the standing American posture and from what the Union has built. **A tightening that only repeats the last tightening is not an event.** This fires up to six times on a single path, and "Washington tightens export licences again, allies are rationed" is the same sentence every time. Each occurrence has to reach somewhere the last one did not, and the reach is what the clipping reports: backwards onto equipment already installed, so renewals, servicing and spare parts need the approvals a new purchase needs; outwards onto the Union's own onward sales, so a buyer must account for who it sells to; off the hardware entirely onto model weights above a capability threshold, which travel under American rules because they were trained on American accelerators; onto people, so secondments, hiring and published research become licensable; and finally onto politics, where allocations follow votes in other forums and the instrument has stopped being trade policy at all. Volume-licence status is the state of the world between tightenings, not the news in one.

events.title: Adoption Delivers
events.description: Public-sector AI adoption produces visible, measurable benefit – waiting lists that fall, decisions that arrive in days rather than months, teaching that demonstrably works – and it is attributed to a European decision rather than to an American product. **Vary what works, and who notices.** This fires on most paths and repeats on two thirds of them, and "waiting lists fall and Brussels gets the credit" is one sentence, not five. Change the sector each time – health, then permits and benefits, then schools, then courts, then the things nobody photographs, like procurement and payroll – and change what the success does politically: the first is a relief, a later one is cited against the Union by people who want the money spent elsewhere, and a later one still is taken for granted and stops being mentioned. Where the same path has already had a success, the new one is measured against it, not announced fresh.

events.title: Joint Threat Response
events.description: States hit by the same class of incident pool attribution, intelligence and response: a joint cyber command with real-time telemetry sharing that the Union is invited into, or a biosurveillance pact with binding sample-sharing and a standing investigation mandate. The Union gains protection it could not build alone, and a seat at tables it was not sitting at. It moves `resilience` on the terms of metric rule 4.

events.title: Middle Powers Coordinate
events.description: A coordination framework among the Union and other middle powers holding pieces of the AI supply chain — export-licence alignment, joint bargaining over compute access, shared evaluation capacity. Nobody cedes sovereignty to it, but together its members can withhold things even the great powers need. It counts as securing access on the terms of metric rule 5, and moves `eu_political_capital` on the terms of metric rule 6.

events.title: emergent_anti_automation_sabotage
events.description: Municipal sabotage wave targets backup power and offline triage kits in several member states as hostility to automation turns physical, degrading local continuity during containment.

events.title: emergent_sabotage_of_resilience_buildout
events.description: Anti-automation municipal bans spread to block grid upgrades and clinic backup-kit depots, delaying repair and containment logistics for weeks.
